title: How do bats fly on wings of skin?
examples: Is a bat's wing like a hand?
How is a bat wing different from a bird wing?
How do bats hang upside down?

explain.say: Bats are the only mammals that truly fly. A bat's wing is its hand: thin, stretchy skin is spread between very long finger bones, the arm, the body and the leg.

draw.text: How do bats fly on wings of skin?

explain.say: A bird's wing is a stiff arm covered in feathers, with the hand bones fused together. A bat's wing has many joints, so the bat can curve, fold and twist it during every wingbeat.
Bats can turn very tightly and even land upside down. Tiny muscles in the skin tune its stiffness, and microscopic hairs on the wing sense the air flowing over it, helping the bat adjust each beat.

explain.say: To land on a ceiling, many bats fly up, flip over and grab on with their feet. Tendons in their toes lock the grip, so hanging upside down while they sleep costs almost no effort.

faq.q: Is a bat's wing like a hand?
faq.a: Yes. A bat's wing has the same bones as your arm and hand, but the finger bones are extremely long and joined by thin skin. The thumb stays free as a small hook for climbing.
asks: What bones are in a bat wing?

faq.q: Why can bats turn so tightly?
faq.a: A bat can bend its many finger joints to change the wing's shape, tiny muscles in the skin adjust its stiffness, and sensitive hairs feel the airflow. Together these let it twist and turn in tight spaces.
asks: How do bats change direction so fast?

faq.q: How is a bat wing different from a bird wing?
faq.a: A bird wing is a stiff arm covered in feathers. A bat wing is skin stretched over long, bendy fingers, so the bat can cup, fold and twist it far more with every beat.

faq.q: How do bats hang upside down without effort?
faq.a: When a bat hangs, its body weight pulls on tendons that lock its toes around the perch. Its muscles can relax, so it can even sleep hanging and stays put without effort.
asks: Why do bats sleep upside down?
How do bats grip the ceiling?

faq.q: How do bats find their way when they fly at night?
faq.a: Most small insect-eating bats use echolocation, listening to the echoes of their own calls. Many fruit bats rely mainly on good eyesight and smell instead.

facts: The scientific name for bats, Chiroptera, means hand-wing.
Bat wings carry tiny touch-sensitive hairs that sense airflow (Sterbing-D'Angelo and colleagues, 2011).

quiz.say: Why does a hanging bat use almost no energy to grip?
quiz.show: Why does a hanging bat use almost no energy to grip?

wrong.1: Bats do not use glue to hang.
